title: Subtree of Another Tree
prompt:
Given the roots of two binary trees `root` and `subRoot`, return `true` if `subRoot` appears as an exact subtree of `root` (a node in `root` whose entire subtree structurally matches `subRoot`, values included), or `false` otherwise.

Both trees are given as level-order arrays where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives both arrays directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds a tree from an array, so you only need to implement the subtree-matching logic.

examples.explanation: The subtree rooted at the node with value 4 exactly matches subRoot.
The node with value 4 has an extra descendant (0) that subRoot doesn't have, so it's not an exact match.
With a single-node root and a single-node subRoot of the same value, the whole tree trivially matches as its own subtree.

constraints: The number of nodes in root is in the range [1, 2000]
The number of nodes in subRoot is in the range [1, 1000]
hints: You already know how to check if two trees are exactly identical (same shape, same values) — reuse that as a helper.
Walk every node of root; at each node, check whether the subtree rooted there is identical to subRoot.
If any node in root passes the identical-tree check against subRoot, the answer is true; if none do after visiting all nodes, it's false.

solution.approach: Write a helper `is_same(a, b)` that checks whether two trees are structurally identical with matching values, exactly like the Same Tree problem. Then traverse every node of `root`; for each node, check if the subtree rooted there is identical to `subRoot`. Return true as soon as one matches, otherwise false after the full traversal.
